envelope.description: Build and package the OS-native stable process-capability broker

body.title: Build and package the OS-native stable process-capability broker
body.summary: Implement the internal local-source broker: Linux opens a pidfd before identity validation and observes/signals only that handle; Darwin acquires a stable Mach task right and validates unique process incarnation before readiness. Denied/unavailable APIs fail closed without privilege changes or PID-kill fallback. Add root build-process-broker.mjs to package.json between tsc and actual root copy-assets.mjs; ship the host executable in out/bin. Runtime requires no compiler or downloaded code. Keep a platform-evidence matrix: Linux runtime results, Darwin denial/unsupported seam results, and Darwin actual runtime status separately. Never describe the feasibility probe or mocks as Darwin validation.
acceptanceChecks: Real Linux disposable-process tests prove handle capture, termination, exit observation and no retargeting after the original exits.
Darwin denied/unsupported capability paths fail closed; Darwin runtime evidence is required before claiming that backend works.
Normal build compiles and packages the local broker; missing toolchain/API produces actionable diagnostics.
No native target-termination path falls back to numeric-PID kill or opens databases/network connections.

tests.name: Native Linux retained-capability capture termination and post-exit non-retargeting
Darwin denied or unsupported capabilities fail closed and runtime evidence remains explicit
Normal build compiles and ships the local broker without a runtime compiler or PID-kill fallback
